children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares fell on Wednesday following an overnight selloff in technology stocks on Wall Street that revived doubts about the sustainability of the AI trade. The won strengthened, while the benchmark bond yield fell.
** The benchmark KOSPI
was down 238.37 points, or 4.76%, at 4,767.66, as of 0154 GMT.

** A lot of profit-taking is taking place after Tuesday's sharp rebound, while the possibility of additional US tariffs is weighing on investor sentiment, said Kang Jin-hyeok, an analyst at Shinhan Investment & Securities.
** Before the rebound, AI-linked stocks had struggled for weeks as investors questioned the sector's debt-fueled spending and the returns it could generate.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
fell 8% on Wednesday, while peer SK Hynix
lost 7.51%.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 1.11%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were down 2.09% and unchanged, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 1.37%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
rose 3.64%.
** Of the total 903 traded issues, 304 shares advanced, while 568 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 1,016.0 billion won.
** The won was quoted at 1,341.6 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.10% higher than its previous close at 1,343.0.
** In offshore trading, the won
was quoted at 1,343.0 per dollar, down 0.2% on the day, while in non-deliverable forward trading its one-month contract (KRW1MNDFOR=) was quoted at 1,341.8.
** The KOSPI has risen 13.13% so far this year.
** The won has strengthened 7.3% against the dollar so far this year.
** In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.04 point to 103.85.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose 0.2 basis points to 3.638%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell 3.2 basis points to 3.791%.
